name: Statistics (Min)

blocks.name: Program Requirements

rules.name: Qualifying Courses
rules.notes:
Note that CME 102 is not a suitable course to use in place of MATH 52; if a student has taken CME 102, they need to take one of the alternative courses to satisfy the Qualifying Course requirement.
MATH 52 can be double-counted between the statistics minor and a major or other minor.

rules.name: Theoretical Statistics Requirement
rules.notes:
Students who take STATS 118 for this Theoretical Statistics Requirement can count STATS 200 or STATS 200Q toward the Elective Course requirement below.
If a student has taken MATH 151 or STATS 116X (as an Elective Course for the statistics minor or for any other program), they are required to take STATS 200 or STATS 200Q to fulfill the Theoretical Statistics Requirement.
STATS 118 has a prerequisite of STATS 117, which can count as an Elective Course below. CS 109, EE 178, and MS&E 120 also satisfy the prerequisite for STATS 118, but these classes may NOT count toward the Elective Courses requirement for the minor.

rules.name: Elective Courses
rules.desc: Students must take 3 elective courses for a total of at least 9 units. (Each course must be taken for a minimum of 3 units.) At least 2 courses must be Advanced Statistics Electives (STATS courses numbered 200 and above), and up to 1 course may be from the lists of Additional Elective Options.

blocks.notes: For any questions about program requirements, please reach out to the Student Services Specialist via email: datasciencemajor-inquiries@lists.stanford.edu.

grading: All courses for the minor must be taken for a letter grade.
policies: The only courses that can be double-counted between the statistics minor and a major or other minor are MATH 52, MATH 62CM, MATH 63DM, and STATS 110. See the university double-counting policy page for more details. Beyond that, students need to find another suitable course to satisfy the requirements of the minor and expand their skill set.
transferPolicy: The program must approve transfer credits before they can be used toward your Statistics minor requirements. It is considered on a case-by-case basis in conversation with the department. See our Transfer Credit page for more information.
reviewNotes: You take a qualifying math course, STATS 118 or 200, STATS 191 or 203, and three electives of at least 3 units each (9 units or more), at least two of them STATS courses numbered 200 and above and at most one from the Additional Elective Options, for 20 units, all letter graded. That MATH 151 or STATS 116X as an elective means taking STATS 200 for theory, and that only MATH 52, 62CM, 63DM and STATS 110 may also count toward another program, are checked by hand.
